newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE SHARES UP OVER 10 PCT ON VOTING CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: RWE SHARES UP OVER 10 PCT ON VOTING CHANGES.

text.p: Ordinary and preference shares in German diversified utility RWE AG rose in pre-bourse trade on Thursday after it said it would abolish multiple voting rights on shares mainly held by local communes.
RWE preference shares were up 9.70 marks, or 14.65 percent, at 75.90 marks in pre-bourse trade, while ordinary shares were up 7.80 marks, or 9.79 percent, at 87.45 marks.
The overall IBIS DAX index was up 45.91 points, or 1.08 percent, at 4,282.97 points.
The multiple voting rights held by the local communes have long been viewed by analysts as an obstacle to institutional and private investors seeking to buy RWE shares.
RWE said on Wednesday that it planned to convert the registered common stock, with additional voting rights, into bearer common shares carrying standard voting rights.

Because voting rights would become available as a result of this move, RWE said holders of preferred shares would be given the option of swapping their shares for common shares with standard voting rights.
RWE said the total number of votes would not change as a result of these measures.
